prediction_definition.forecast_checkpoint: midpoint of local static sos/eos calendar

decisions: Parse the start year from planting_year labels of the form YYYY/YY.
Map SOS to the first year in planting_year; map EOS to that year unless eos < sos, then use the following year.
Round fractional DOY to the nearest calendar day (floor(doy + 0.5)); retain source SOS/EOS unchanged.
Set cutoff to start_date plus floor(season_duration_days / 2).
Use early/mid/late thirds as generic season phases, not named phenological stages.
Retain planting_date/harvest_date source labels, but do not parse them as exact dates because their day-level semantics are undocumented.
Treat source date as an availability proxy because no publication timestamp is supplied.
Do not replace missing crop calendars with a national or neighboring-region calendar.
assumptions: The first year in planting_year is the calendar year of SOS; local labels all imply harvest_year = start_year + 1.
Static SOS/EOS are a typical seasonal window and approximate each historical campaign.
Harvest date is not equated with EOS; EOS is the end of growing season.
Observation date is used as the information cutoff proxy; publication latency is not represented in the source files.

findings.issue: Some yield admin-season rows have no crop_calendar entry.
findings.action: Keep those target rows; their midseason cutoff and season phase remain null.

findings.issue: Non-wrapping calendars can end in the start year while yield harvest is reported in the following year.
findings.action: Keep separate SOS/EOS growing-season dates from yield harvest dates.

findings.issue: meteorology contains admin units without yield campaigns.
findings.action: Retain source observations; they cannot form supervised yield rows without target data.

findings.issue: meteorology has no in-campaign observations for some yield admin units with calendars.
findings.action: Distinguish source temporal coverage from within-season observation gaps before creating training rows; do not impute here.
